about: Refund programs Upmore can check a refund notice against (packages/domain/84-money-owed.js). A notice is called real only when its sender's domain, or a named administrator's domain, matches an entry here; anything else is 'can't confirm this is real'. Each entry carries its source page and the day its facts were checked; facts come only from the owner's method cards (docs/methods, checked October 2026). A field nobody has checked is null or marked unverified, never filled in from memory as fact. Re-check each entry on its page monthly; past fresh_days it is said as 'may have changed'.

programs.name: the FTC's Amazon refunds
programs.administrators_note: No refund administrator is on file yet: until one is added from the FTC page, only a sender on ftc.gov counts as matching.
programs.stated: Amazon owes some Prime members up to $200 each from a $1.5 billion fund. Payments run through April 2027 and expire after 60 days. The FTC sends refunds by check, PayPal or Venmo, and some expire if not accepted in time.
programs.eligibility_note: Who is eligible is on the program's page; no enrollment window is on file until someone checks it there, so Upmore does not match past charges to this program.

programs.name: the FTC's AT&T data throttling refunds
programs.administrators_note: No refund administrator is on file yet: until one is added from the FTC page, only a sender on ftc.gov counts as matching.
programs.stated: In 2026 the FTC's AT&T round sends Zelle payments to former customers. These people never cashed a check or accepted PayPal.
